decision_text: Raised prices 40% across all tiers to fix negative unit economics.
outcome: Lost 22% of MRR to churn within 60 days; net revenue dropped for 2 months before stabilizing.
lesson: A 40% jump in a commodity SMB category triggered switching; a phased or segmented increase would likely have held more revenue.

decision_text: Raised prices 15% for new customers only, grandfathered existing accounts.
outcome: No measurable churn increase; new-customer margin improved within one quarter.
lesson: Grandfathering existing customers avoided the switching-cost trigger seen in blanket increases.

decision_text: Hired a 3-person outbound sales team before confirming repeatable product-market fit.
outcome: Outbound generated zero qualified pipeline in 4 months; runway dropped from 9 to 4 months before the team was let go.
lesson: Sales-led motion cannot substitute for unproven product-market fit; founder-led validation should have preceded hiring.

decision_text: Delayed all sales hiring for 6 months to run founder-led outbound first, validating messaging before hiring.
outcome: Founder closed 6 deals solo in 6 months, establishing a repeatable pitch; the first sales hire ramped to productivity in under 6 weeks.
lesson: Founder-led validation before hiring compressed the new hire's ramp time significantly.

decision_text: Raised a $1.5M seed round and doubled headcount from 5 to 10 within 2 months.
outcome: New hires took 4-5 months to ramp with no dedicated onboarding lead; growth rate fell to 3%/mo during the ramp period and burn multiple worsened to 3.1x.
lesson: Doubling headcount without an ops/onboarding lead in place created a productivity gap that ate most of the new runway.

decision_text: Raised a $2M Series A and hired in 3 staggered tranches of 2-3 people over 9 months, each tied to a revenue milestone.
outcome: Growth rate held steady through each hiring wave; runway extended to 22 months by month 9.
lesson: Tying hiring tranches to revenue milestones avoided the ramp-time cash crunch seen in single-wave hiring.

decision_text: Pivoted from B2B analytics to a B2C personal-finance app after 3 months of flat B2B growth.

context_at_decision.market: B2B analytics, pivoting to consumer finance
context_at_decision.competitive_position: weak in B2B; crowded in target B2C market

outcome: B2C user acquisition cost ran 4x the modeled estimate; the team burned through the pivot's allotted runway with no path to profitability and shut down 5 months later.
lesson: Pivoting into a crowded consumer category without a distribution advantage repeated the same problem (no differentiated acquisition channel) in a new market.

decision_text: Pivoted from generic project-management SaaS to a niche vertical (construction subcontractor scheduling) after 4 months of flat growth.

context_at_decision.market: generic PM SaaS, pivoting to construction-vertical PM
context_at_decision.competitive_position: weak in generic market; no direct competitor in the narrow vertical

outcome: Existing customer base converted at 40%; new vertical-specific leads closed at 3x the prior rate due to purpose-built features.
lesson: Narrowing into an underserved vertical (rather than a broader adjacent market) let existing product investment carry over.

decision_text: Expanded into the UK/EU market with a $500k budget over 12 months, hiring 2 local sales reps.

context_at_decision.competitive_position: strong in US, no presence in target region

outcome: EU CAC ran 2.5x the US baseline for the first 8 months due to unfamiliar buying processes and compliance requirements; EU revenue reached only 12% of the modeled target by month 12.
lesson: Underestimated regulatory/compliance friction (GDPR, local payroll law) extended the sales cycle well beyond the US benchmark used to model CAC.

decision_text: Expanded into the UK market only (not full EU) with a $200k budget, partnering with a local reseller instead of hiring direct sales.

context_at_decision.competitive_position: strong in US, no presence in target region

outcome: Reseller partnership reached breakeven on the regional investment by month 7; CAC ran close to the US baseline since the reseller absorbed the local relationship-building cost.
lesson: A narrower initial market plus a local partner avoided paying the full compliance/relationship-building cost directly.

decision_text: Ignored a well-funded competitor's aggressive price cuts for 6 months, maintaining premium pricing.

context_at_decision.competitive_position: premium positioning vs. newly aggressive low-cost entrant

outcome: Growth rate fell to 1%/mo as price-sensitive segments switched to the competitor; had to eventually cut prices reactively at a worse negotiating position.
lesson: Delaying a pricing response to competitive pressure let the competitor establish switching momentum before any counter-move.

decision_text: Responded to a competitor's price cuts within 3 weeks by adding a lower-cost tier rather than cutting core pricing.

context_at_decision.competitive_position: premium positioning vs. newly aggressive low-cost entrant

outcome: Churn to the competitor stayed under 5%; the new lower tier captured price-sensitive prospects without discounting the core product.
lesson: A fast, differentiated response (new tier, not a blanket cut) preserved both price-sensitive and premium segments.

decision_text: Raised a $3M Series A pre-revenue, based on a strong prototype and team pedigree.
outcome: Spent 14 months finding product-market fit with no revenue signal to guide iteration; the Series A round's valuation created pressure that led to two rushed, reversed pivots.
lesson: Raising growth-stage capital before any revenue signal removed the forcing function that would have kept iteration grounded in real usage.

decision_text: Raised a smaller $800k pre-seed instead of a larger round, specifically to reach initial revenue before a bigger raise.
outcome: Reached $15k MRR within 7 months on the smaller round; raised a $2.5M Series A at a materially better valuation once revenue existed.
lesson: Deliberately raising less pre-revenue preserved both equity and the discipline to find a real signal before scaling spend.

decision_text: Expanded from one product to three simultaneous product lines to capture more of the market in a single push.
outcome: None of the three product lines reached meaningful traction; engineering and support load tripled while revenue grew only 20% over 6 months.
lesson: Splitting an 8-person team across three products diluted execution below the threshold needed for any one to gain traction.

decision_text: Stayed focused on a single product line and turned down two adjacent-market expansion opportunities to keep the team concentrated.
outcome: Grew to $95k MRR over the following 12 months with the same headcount, then expanded into one adjacent product only after the core reached profitability.
lesson: Concentrating the team on one product until it was self-sustaining created the capacity to expand later without diluting the core.

decision_text: Cut prices 20% to try to out-compete on price against a much larger, better-funded incumbent.

context_at_decision.competitive_position: small player vs. dominant, well-funded incumbent

outcome: The incumbent matched the price cut within weeks using their larger margin cushion; the startup's margin collapsed while growth stayed flat.
lesson: Competing on price against a better-capitalized incumbent invited a price war the smaller company couldn't sustain.

decision_text: Declined to compete on price against a larger incumbent, instead narrowing focus to a specific underserved customer segment the incumbent ignored.

context_at_decision.competitive_position: small player vs. dominant, well-funded incumbent

outcome: Grew 3x within a year inside the underserved segment, where the incumbent's generic product was a poor fit and did not respond competitively.
lesson: Avoiding a direct price fight and finding a segment the incumbent structurally couldn't serve well was more durable than competing head-on.
